prompt: Complete a Thermostat class whose target temperature starts at 20.0 and whose setTarget method clamps any requested value into the range 10.0 to 30.0.
explanation: A setter is the natural place to enforce an invariant: by clamping inside setTarget, the field can never hold an out-of-range value no matter what callers pass in. This is encapsulation in action -- the private field plus a validating setter guarantees the object stays in a valid state. Math.min and Math.max can express the same clamp in one line.
hints: Assign 20.0 to the target field inside the no-argument constructor.
In setTarget, use if/else if to raise values below 10.0 and lower values above 30.0 before storing.
Equivalent one-liner: target = Math.max(10.0, Math.min(30.0, value));
